findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined for this bucket, so objects (including the seeded vendor roster) are stored without enforced SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 encryption at rest.

findings.issue_category: missing access control / public access block
findings.description: No ACL is specified and there is no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or restrictive bucket policy, leaving the bucket without explicit access control and vulnerable to accidental public exposure via ACLs or policies.
The bucket holding report data has no logging block, so object-level access to potentially sensitive data cannot be audited or attributed during an incident.
Versioning is not enabled, so object overwrites or malicious/accidental deletions are unrecoverable; combined with force_destroy = true the bucket and its contents can be destroyed without safeguard.
The ledger export bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so financial export data is stored unencrypted at the bucket-default level.
No logging block is configured for this bucket, leaving access to ledger exports unaudited.
Versioning is disabled while force_destroy = true, so ledger export objects can be overwritten or permanently deleted with no recovery path, undermining data integrity controls.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so model artifacts are stored without enforced default encryption at rest.
The runbooks bucket, which commonly contains operational procedures and sensitive internal detail, has no default server-side encryption configured.
No logging block is configured, so reads and writes to operational runbooks are not recorded for audit or intrusion detection.

The ACL is set to "lcatalogopts-delivery-write", which is not a valid S3 canned ACL (the intended value is presumably "log-delivery-write"). A malformed access-control setting on the log-target bucket means the intended delivery permissions are not correctly and deliberately applied.

The bucket that receives access logs for model_artifacts has force_destroy = true and no object-lock/MFA-delete protection, allowing audit evidence to be wiped in a single destroy operation, which weakens tamper-evidence of the logging trail.

A vendor roster spreadsheet (likely containing third-party PII/business data) is uploaded to a bucket with no default encryption and no explicit kms_key_id or server_side_encryption argument on the object, so it is stored in cleartext.
